title: Portable generated C++ standard compatibility
objective: Make generated FFLAS exception-shim adapters compile on Apple Clang/libc++ arm64 by selecting the oldest portable supported C++ language standard consistently across Unix, Xcode, and MSVC without changing pure-C kernels, with deterministic binding.gyp regression coverage and real macOS validation.

oracles: real Apple Clang 17 arm64 package build
exceptions: Generated C++ foreign-library exception shields require an explicit portable language standard.

handoff.summary: Generated native kernels with C++ exception shields now select C++17 explicitly and consistently: `-std=c++17` for Unix compilers, `CLANG_CXX_LANGUAGE_STANDARD: c++17` for Xcode, and `LanguageStandard: stdcpp17` for MSVC. Pure-C kernels retain their previous recipes. The compiler exposes and uses one inspectable language-standard policy, while deterministic tests exercise the actual generated `binding.gyp` structure for Linux, macOS, and Windows. A clean generated FFLAS host adapter was built on an Apple M1 Max with Apple Clang 17; its emitted recipe contained both Unix and Xcode C++17 settings, and all eight FFLAS/FFPACK package tests passed.
risks: The portable tier was run and its mathematical/compiler tests passed, but its manifest ratchet has one inherited integration failure: `test/exact-matrix-scalar-operations.cjs` exists on the base branch without an entry in `test/node-test-manifest.cjs`. This lane does not claim either file.

Windows x64 and Linux arm64 recipes are covered deterministically at the generated `binding.gyp` level; their real compiler builds remain CI/integration validation rather than lane-local hardware tests.
next_steps: Register the inherited exact-matrix scalar test in the integration lane, then rerun `pnpm test:portable`.
Retain Windows x64 and Linux arm64 native package builds as release/CI gates.
